The device should now reboot itself and connect to the specific Wifi/MQTT broker. \n\nWhen the connection succeeds, the device LED will turn solid green. That means the device has paired successfully. If that does not happen, then you need to start over again and double check Wifi configuration, MQTT configuration and Credentials configuration.
Congratulations! The pairing process completed successfully and the HTTP API reported the device online. You should be ready to go.

Put your Meross device in Pairing mode and then tap on the update button.\n\nBe sure to enable both Wifi and Location (GPS) access on your device. Some devices also require to turn off HotSpot in case it\'s active.
Please select the WiFi AP where the Meross device should connect to.
Log-in to the HTTP API broker.
Make sure the Meross Local Broker (on HomeAssistant) Addon is started and log-in using the credentials configured in the configuration section of that Addon.
Meross plugs are only capable to connect to MQTT over TLS connections (default port 8883). Using a clear-mqtt connection won\'t work.

Use this option to manually set the UserId and Key values manually. Such values are usually provided by the Meross HTTP API broker or by the HA Local Addon. However, you can manually set such values in case you want to pair against third-party brokers: you sure know what you are doing.
Meross Local Pairer configures Meross devices to use a local MQTT broker instead of the Meross cloud. It works with the Meross Local Broker Home Assistant add-on and the meross-cloud integration.
Meross Local Pairer is developed and maintained by mazkagaz.

Meross Local Pairer is an unofficial fork of Alberto Geniola\'s Custom Pairer. The original protocol and application were created by Alberto Geniola. This fork fixes response validation, custom credential handling, provisioning reliability and security issues.
